claim.pdf_says: The PDF prints the two paragraphs "If any of the LINE clauses used in computing the trial sum are subject to a PRESENT WHEN clause ..." and "If the trial sum is less than or equal to the lower limit for the report group, the page fit is declared successful; ..." indented under item c) of 13.16.33.3 GR4, and prints "If the page fit was declared successful, no page advance takes place and the report group is printed on the current page; ..." back at the rule-4 body indent, so it applies to all three forms a), b) and c) of the page fit test.
claim.markdown_says:
If any of the LINE clauses used in computing the trial sum are subject to a PRESENT WHEN clause ...

   If the trial sum is less than or equal to the lower limit for the report group, the page fit is declared successful; ...

   If the page fit was declared successful, no page advance takes place and the report group is printed on the current page; ...
claim.why_it_matters: All three paragraphs carry the same 3-space indent as the a)/b)/c) items, so the transcription no longer distinguishes c)'s continuation paragraphs from the closing paragraph of GR4. A reader can take the page-advance consequence as part of item c) (relative LINE only) rather than the outcome of every page fit test form, including a) NEXT PAGE and b) absolute LINE.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (p.301 of the 2002 standard) does indent the two trial-sum paragraphs under c) and outdents 'If the page fit was declared successful...' to the rule-4 body margin, as claimed. The markdown carries every paragraph, word for word, in the same order; only the indentation is flattened, and it is flattened uniformly: the rule-4 body paragraphs ('The nature of the page fit test...', 'The page fit test takes one of the following forms:') and the a)/b)/c) items all share the same 3-space indent, so the markdown encodes no nesting depth anywhere in this rule. Nothing is missing, misplaced or reordered. The scope is not changed in meaning: the closing paragraph speaks generically of 'the page fit was declared successful', which a) and b) also declare, and a) and b) would have no consequence at all if it belonged to c) alone, so the reading the claim fears does not follow from the text. This is a layout/indent difference, not a content discrepancy.
